# What Is GPT (and GPT-4o)? A Plain English Explanation for Australian Small Business

## Everyone’s using ChatGPT. Almost nobody knows what GPT actually means.

You’ve probably typed something into ChatGPT. Maybe you use it every day. But if someone asked you to explain what GPT stands for, and more importantly, what it actually does, would you know?

Most people wouldn’t. And that’s fine. You don’t need to know how a car engine works to drive. But understanding the basics of GPT helps you use these tools smarter, especially when you’re deciding whether to pay for a subscription, which AI product to trust, or why the output you’re getting is sometimes brilliant and sometimes completely wrong.

## The plain English version

GPT stands for Generative Pre-trained Transformer. Each word is doing real work here.

Generative means it generates new text rather than retrieving stored answers. When you ask ChatGPT something, it doesn’t look up the answer in a database, it constructs a response, word by word, based on patterns it learned during training.

Pre-trained means the model learned from a massive amount of text before you ever used it. Books, websites, code, articles, billions of words. That training happened once (at enormous cost and computing power). What you’re doing when you chat with it is using that pre-trained knowledge, not teaching it new things in real time.

Transformer is the architecture, the underlying design of how the model processes language. Transformers were invented in 2017 and turned out to be spectacularly good at understanding context and relationships between words. Every major AI language model today uses some version of this design.

GPT-4o (pronounced “four-oh”) is OpenAI’s current flagship model. The “o” stands for “omni”, meaning it can handle text, images, and audio in a single model. GPT-4o is what powers the paid tier of ChatGPT.

## Why it matters for Australian small businesses

When you hear “GPT,” you’re usually hearing a shorthand for any large language model, the tech behind ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and dozens of other tools. It’s become the category name the same way “Google” became the verb for searching.

What matters practically:

- GPT models have a knowledge cutoff, they stop learning at a certain date. GPT-4o’s training cut off in early 2024. Anything after that, it doesn’t know unless it has web access turned on.
- GPT models hallucinate, they generate plausible-sounding text even when they’re wrong. It’s structural to how they work, and it won’t disappear in a future update.
- Newer GPT versions are generally more capable, but also cost more to run, which affects what you get on free vs paid plans.

For an Australian business owner, this means: ChatGPT is a genuinely useful tool for drafting, summarising, and thinking through problems. It’s not a reliable source of facts, prices, regulations, or anything time-sensitive.

## A real Australian example

A marketing consultant in Sydney uses GPT-4o every day to write first drafts of client emails, rewrite website copy, and brainstorm campaign angles. She’s probably cut her drafting time in half.

She also knows better than to ask it whether a particular claim is legal under Australian Consumer Law, or what the current GST rate is. For that, she checks with an accountant or looks at the ATO website. GPT is her writing partner, not her compliance officer.

That’s the mental model worth keeping: GPT is a writing and thinking tool, not a facts database.

## What to do with this knowledge

You don’t need to understand transformers to use ChatGPT well. But knowing that it’s generating text (not retrieving facts) helps you use it correctly.

Use it to draft, rewrite, brainstorm, summarise, and explain. Treat everything it tells you as a starting point, not a final answer. Verify anything factual before you rely on it. And if you’re comparing AI tools, “which version of GPT does this use?” is a legitimate question to ask, because the model underneath matters.

# OpenAI 最强模型 GPT-5 来了，免费可用

频道：区块链行情 日期： 浏览：1

撰文：李丹，华尔街见闻

今年 OpenAI 最为大众期待的产品来了。

美东时间 8 月 7 日周四，OpenAI 宣布，推出新一代旗舰人工智能（AI）模型 GPT-5。它是 OpenAI 首个「一体化」的 AI 系统，是 OpenAI 首次将 o 系列模型的推理能力与 GPT 系列模型快速响应能力相结合的产物。

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman 在新模型发布会上高度评价 GPT-5，称它是「世界上最好的模型」，是相比此前模型的「重大升级」，并表示，它的问世标志着，OpenAI 在实现通用人工智能（AGI）道路上迈出「重要一步」。

OpenAI 介绍，GPT-5 在多项基准测试中表现出色，在编程、数学、健康等领域达到前沿水平。GPT-5 在 SWE-bench Verified 代码测试中得到 74.9% 的准确率，略超 Anthropic 本周二发布的新模型 Claude Opus 4.1。同时，GPT-5 的幻觉问题大幅改善，错误信息率仅为 4.8%，远低于前代模型 GPT-4o 的 20.6%。

从本周四当日起，GPT-5 向所有 ChatGPT 的免费用户和订阅 Plus、Pro、Team 的付费用户开放，作为默认模型使用，并于一周内在 Enterprise 和 Edu 付费方案上线。

与 GPT-4o 一样，GPT-5 免费和付费版的区别在于用量。Plus 用户享有更高使用限额，Pro 用户可无限使用并获得增强版本 GPT-5 Pro。对于免费用户，完整的推理功能可能需要几天时间才能全部上线。一旦免费用户达到 GPT-5 的用量限制，OpenAI 就将为他们切换到更小的模型 GPT-5 mini。

OpenAI 周三还表示，将以每年 1 美元的象征性收费向美国联邦政府机构提供 ChatGPT 产品。具体来说是 ChatGPT 的企业版，其中包含强化的安全和隐私功能。

OpenAI 刚刚官宣 GPT-5，微软就宣布，从本周四开始，将 GPT-5 整合到旗下广泛的产品组合中，包括 365 Copilot、Copilot、GitHub Copilot 和 Azure AI Foundry 等平台，让微软的企业和消费者用户能够立即体验到 GPT-5 的高级推理能力和编程优势。
GPT-5 拥有编程、创意写作、健康领域三大优势
OpenAI 的 GPT5 发布公告在一开头就说，GPT-5 是 OpenAI「最智能、最快速、最实用的模型，其内置的思维能力，让每个人都能拥有专家级的智慧。」

根据 OpenAI 介绍，作为 OpenAI 的「最强大模型」，GPT-5 在三个关键领域实现了显著提升。

首先是编程能力。GPT-5 是 OpenAI 迄今为止最强大的编码模型，在复杂的前端生成和大型代码库调试方面表现突出，能够仅凭一个提示就创建美观响应式的网站、应用程序 App 和游戏。早期测试者注意到其在间距、排版和留白等设计选择方面的改进。

在从 GitHub 获取现实世界编码任务的基准测试 SWE-bench Verified 中，GPT-5 思考后首次尝试的准确率达 74.9%，高于 OpenAI 推理模型 o3 的 69.1% 和 GPT-4o 的 30.8%。

# Google 發表 Gemini 4 Carbon！資安三基準全面領先、Intelligence Index 59 分奪冠

Google DeepMind 推出下一代 frontier 模型 Gemini 4 Carbon，Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 拿下第一、資安基準全面領先，卻仍先開放給資安防禦夥伴與政府審測。
（前情提要：Google 發表 Gemini 4 Argon！空間推理大進化、驅動 Apollo 人形機器人，API 定價出爐）
（背景補充：Anthropic 傳本月發表新模型！Google Gemini 4 Carbon 同步備戰，OpenAI 新 Terra 也可能跟進）

本文目錄

Google DeepMind 於美國時間 10 月 28 日公布 Gemini 4 Carbon，定位為下一代 frontier 模型，強調資安與長時程（long horizon）能力達到目前最強水準。這款模型建立在兩週前發布的 Gemini 4 Argon 之上，由 Google DeepMind 資深副總裁暨 Google 首席 AI 架構師 Koray Kavukcuoglu 署名說明。

在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0，Carbon 以 59 分居冠；資安相關基準亦全面領先，顯示 Google 把「防禦向」能力當成這一輪的主軸賣點。

### 資安三環與長時程代理工程同步升級

官方在無護欄條件下公布的資安數據為：SEC-bench Pro 找漏洞 88.2%、ExploitGym 利用驗證 54.8%、CWE-bench 修補 71.0%，分別對應發現、驗證、修復三個環節。內部測試顯示，產生安全程式碼的成功率相對 Argon 逾 2 倍；Chrome 團隊稱，Carbon 產出高品質修補的表現，較另一家實驗室的前沿模型好逾 10 倍；雲端資安業者 Wiz 也觀察到它在 web 滲透測試基準上領先。

編碼與代理面，Carbon 被設計成能撐多日的 agentic 工程流程，例如在大型程式碼庫與底層系統裡追根因、補洞。WebDev Arena 分數上漲 89 elo，來到第 4 名（1769），全端網頁與多模態理解也被點名改善。

安全對齊方面，Terminal-Bench 4.0 成功作弊降到 0.0%、作弊嘗試 0.4%；內部高優先對齊警報約減近 80%；無根據聲稱相對 Argon 約砍半；越權減少 26%、服務不足減少 29%；Gray Swan 間接提示注入（IPI）攻擊成功率為 0.0%，Argon 當時為 0.7%。

### 能力領先，仍先鎖資安夥伴與政府審測

儘管跑分與內部回饋都偏強，Google 強調審慎釋出：正參與美國政府自願上市前測試；本週起先給一部分 cyber defenders，再經 Fairwind Program 逐步開放給信任夥伴，開發者、企業與消費者則「盡快」經產品介面上線。

這套節奏與 Argon 當時「跑分領先、一般用戶卻暫不能直接用」高度相似 —— 雙用風險下，Google 寧可先把最強能力放在防禦端與可控夥伴圈，再談全面鋪開。

### 兩週再推一代，導入價先對齊 Argon

對開發者與資安防禦團隊來說，Carbon 意味著「能長時間跑工程代理、又能幫找洞與修洞」的工具密度再抬一階；對模型競賽節奏則是訊號：Argon 才上兩週又推 Carbon，前沿迭代已壓縮到以週為單位。

定價與 Argon 導入期相同：輸入每百萬 token 2 美元、輸出 10 美元，快取輸入再打 95% 折；導入期結束後調為輸入 4 美元、輸出 20 美元。換句話說，這一輪拼的是能力與釋出節奏，不是先用價格戰搶市。

Arena.ai最新榜单也显示，其在Text Arena登顶第一、Agent Arena位列第二。

核心能力上，Gemini 4 Carbon重点升级长时程工程与网络安全两大方向。

长时程任务上，模型可连续运行数天处理大型代码库与底层系统问题，自主定位并修复隐蔽软件缺陷，在多项编程与智能体基准测试中处于行业第一梯队。

开放节奏与定价方面，该模型本周优先向少量网络安全防御人员开放，后续通过合作计划逐步扩容，普通用户与开发者的全面开放暂无明确时间表。

该发布方式也引发讨论，不少业内观点认为，头部厂商频繁发布却迟迟不落地的模式更偏向榜单竞争，实际落地价值仍需大众体验验证。

Google.content:
## Gemini 4 Carbon正式发布，哈基米重回世界第一

Gemini 终于又支棱起来了。

当全世界的目光都聚焦在苹果首款触控屏 MacBook Pro 身上，Google DeepMind 刚刚正式宣布推出新一代旗舰模型 Gemini 4 Carbon。

按照官方公布的数据，Gemini 4 Carbon 在最新 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 榜单中拿下 59 分，超越 Claude Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6 Astra，登上全球大模型榜首。

更惊人的是，Gemini 4 Carbon 已经能连续数天处理复杂工程任务，自主寻找、验证并修复软件安全漏洞，在多项网络安全基准测试中刷新纪录。

然而，如此强大的模型，普通用户暂时还用不上：谷歌决定优先向少数网络安全防御人员开放，其他用户何时能够体验仍没有明确时间表。

重回世界第一，Gemini 也开始卷能力上限了

回顾今年的大模型竞争，谷歌的更新节奏明显正在「知耻而后勇」。

此前，接连推出 Gemini Flash 3.5 至 3.8 系列后，谷歌迟迟没有兑现新一代旗舰 Pro 模型的期待。另一边，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 持续刷新能力上限，国产模型也在不断追赶，谷歌急需一款有分量的产品重新证明自己的实力。

直到两周前前，Gemini 4 Argon 才终于上线。

Argon 意为「氩」，是一种性质稳定的惰性气体，常用于焊接和半导体制造中的保护环境。Argon 在文笔写作、表达质量等方面取得了明显提升，但距离全面领先顶级模型仍有差距。

如今，谷歌又带来了 Carbon，也就是「碳」。作为构成生命与有机化合物的重要元素，碳既能形成柔软的石墨，也能构成坚硬的金刚石。（PS：照这个更新速度，元素周期表跟产品路线图没什么区别了）

真正让 Gemini 4 Carbon 引起关注的，还是它公布的一系列成绩。

就在 10 月 27 日，独立模型评测机构 Artificial Analysis 刚刚升级了 Intelligence Index v5.0。这套综合指数涵盖知识工作、编程、科学和通用推理四大领域，各占 25%，其中 60% 的评测权重采用私有测试数据或隐藏答案，进一步提高了测试难度。

昨天新版榜单发布时，Claude Opus 5.5 以 58 分排名第一，GPT-6 Astra 以 57 分紧随其后，GPT-6.1 Sol 则以 55 分位居第三。而 Gemini 4 Carbon 直接拿到了 59 分，比 Argon 高出 9 分，也以 1 分优势超过此前榜首的 Claude Opus 5.5。

不止 Artificial Analysis，Arena.ai 最新公布的榜单也显示，Gemini 4 Carbon（High）在 Text Arena 登顶第一、Agent Arena 排名第二、Code Arena WebDev 排名第四。

伴随着新模型登顶，谷歌内部也开始为 Gemini 积极造势。此前从 Anthropic 跳槽至 Google DeepMind 的华人研究员姚顺宇，同样为 Gemini 系列宣传打 call。

除了综合排名，Gemini 4 Carbon 在实际工程任务上的表现也有明显变化。

过去，大模型可以在几分钟内写出一段程序，但面对大型软件工程，问题就复杂得多。一个隐藏在数百个文件中的故障，可能需要开发者反复检查依赖关系、定位异常、修改代码，再经过多轮测试才能解决。

对于 AI 而言，难点除了编程能力，还有能否在长时间执行任务的过程中保持目标一致，并在失败之后继续尝试。

谷歌表示，Gemini 4 Carbon 已经能够连续运行数天，处理大型代码库和底层系统中的复杂工程问题，即使遇到障碍，也能持续寻找其他方案，最终定位并修复一些隐蔽的软件缺陷。

网页开发方面，Gemini 4 Carbon 在 WebDev Arena 上的 Elo 评分提升了 89 分，达到 1769 分，排名第四。

相比过去随叫随到的编程助手，谷歌希望 Gemini 4 Carbon 能够成为真正承担复杂工程任务的自主 Agent。

不过，前代 Gemini 4 Argon 虽然能力有所提升，但实际使用时额度消耗较快，稍微处理几个复杂任务，就可能触及使用限制。希望这一代 Carbon 在提升能力上限的同时，也能改善额度消耗和使用限制问题。

AI 开始自主寻找、利用和修复漏洞

如果说长程编程体现了 Gemini 4 Carbon 的工程能力，那么网络安全，可能才是谷歌此次更新最值得关注的部分。

传统的软件安全工作需要经历多个环节，首先从大量代码中寻找漏洞，再判断漏洞是否真的可以利用，最后针对问题编写修复程序，并验证修改是否有效。

Gemini 4 Carbon 的能力提升，恰好覆盖了这条完整流程。

在 SEC-bench Pro 测试中，Gemini 4 Carbon 取得了 88.2% 的成绩，主要考察模型在真实软件中自主发现复杂漏洞的能力；

在 ExploitGym 测试中，Gemini 4 Carbon 达到 54.8%，重点考察能否实际利用漏洞来验证风险；

在 Collinear 的 CWE-bench 测试中，Gemini 4 Carbon 又取得 71.0%，能够针对发现的问题生成有效的代码修复方案。

按照谷歌披露的结果，Gemini 4 Carbon 在上述三项测试中均达到了领先水平，相关成绩是在未启用安全防护限制的条件下测得。

谷歌内部测试也给出了相似结果。

在安全代码生成方面，Gemini 4 Carbon 的成功率超过 Argon 的两倍；Chrome 团队发现，其生成高质量安全补丁的表现比另一家实验室的前沿模型高出十倍以上，但未披露对比对象。谷歌旗下云安全平台 Wiz 也观察到，Carbon 在网络应用渗透测试中取得领先成绩。

从发现漏洞、验证风险到完成修复，AI 正在逐渐掌握网络安全专家的一整套工作流程。但同样的能力既能用于修复系统，也可能被攻击者利用，因此，谷歌还重点提升了 Carbon 在自主执行任务时的可靠性。

在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 测试中，Carbon 成功作弊的比例降至 0.0%，尝试作弊的比例仅为 0.4%，同时任务准确率有所提升。

在实际编程环境中，高严重程度的行为不一致警报减少近 80%，缺乏证据支持的断言减少约一半，越权行动和未充分完成任务的情况也分别下降 26% 和 29%。

另一项进展来自提示词注入防护。

攻击者可能在网页或文档中植入恶意指令，诱导 AI 偏离原本任务，而在 Gray Swan 的间接提示词注入测试中，Carbon 将攻击成功率从 Argon 的 0.7% 进一步降至 0.0%，抵御了此次测试覆盖的全部攻击尝试。

当然，测试中的零成功率并不意味着现实中的所有攻击都能被阻止。有 Hacker News 网友认为，减少 AI 在执行任务时投机取巧，可能是提升前沿模型实用性的重要进步之一。

毕竟，当 AI 开始自主处理复杂工程任务，人们除了关心它能否完成工作，还必须考虑它会不会越权操作、编造结果，甚至在遇到障碍时擅自行动。

AI 圈最时髦的营销，是无实物表演

不过，Gemini 4 Carbon 发布后，最引人关注的争议，反而和模型能力没有太大关系。

按照官方安排，Gemini 4 Carbon 本周将首先提供给部分网络安全防御人员，再通过 Fairwind Program 逐步扩大至可信合作伙伴。谷歌表示正在审慎参与美国政府自愿开展的模型发布前测试，至于普通开发者和消费者何时能够使用，暂时没有时间表。

价格方面，Gemini 4 Carbon 将沿用 Argon 的首发定价，每百万输入 Token 收费 2 美元，输出 Token 收费 10 美元，缓存输入优惠 95%。推广期结束后，标准价格将调整为输入 4 美元、输出 20 美元。

值得一提的是，谷歌发布新模型的消息传到 Hacker News，评论区很快热闹起来。

不少网友直言，自己越来越反感谷歌提前宣布新模型、却迟迟不开放的做法；也有网友表示，已经懒得点开谷歌的模型发布链接，因为最后总会发现产品暂时用不上。

不知道从什么时候开始，AI 厂商们似乎越来越擅长一种奇特的发布方式。

原本等打磨好就能直接端上桌的旗舰模型，现在非要套上一层能力太强怕毁灭世界的安全叙事外壳，隔三差五发篇通稿围猎大伙的注意力，结果到头来却迟迟用不上。

这种「无实物表演」的发布方式属实是被 Anthropic 带到沟里去了。

归根结底，争抢全球第一 AI 头衔的竞争，也确实越来越像一场营销游戏。在一个模型几乎每隔几天就会刷新的时代，发布越来越容易，真正让用户相信它有多强，反而越来越难。

毕竟，Benchmark 可以告诉我们模型在考试中有多厉害，但能否进入真实的工作环境、创造持续的价值，还得等用户真正用上它之后才知道。

而对于 Gemini 来说，或许比再次宣布全球第一更重要的事情，是尽快让这个全球第一让更多人有机会用上。

# Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon with enhanced coding, cybersecurity capabilities

The new AI model claims improved performance in vulnerability detection, secure coding and complex multi-step tasks
 AGENCY 
29 Oct 2026 08:01am

AFP Photo

ISTANBUL – Google has announced its latest artificial intelligence (AI) model, Gemini 4 Carbon, claiming significant improvements in coding, agentic tasks and cybersecurity defence, Anadolu Ajansi reported.

Unveiled just two weeks after the launch of its Gemini 4 Argon model, the company described Carbon in a blog post as its strongest frontier model, with advanced cybersecurity capabilities and the ability to handle complex, long-running tasks.

Google attributed the rapid release to its researchers and AI models "working hand in hand to advance capabilities faster".

The company said Gemini 4 Carbon ranked first on the updated version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, scoring 59.

Based on user feedback from its previous release, Google said it had improved the model's performance in full-stack web development, scientific tasks and multimodal understanding. It also claimed the model had gained 89 points to rank fourth on the WebDev Arena leaderboard.

In cybersecurity benchmarks, Google said the model delivered leading results, scoring 88.2 per cent on SEC-bench Pro for identifying vulnerabilities, 54.8 per cent on ExploitGym for exploiting vulnerabilities and 71 per cent on CWE-bench for patching them.

"On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates," the company said.

On safety and alignment, Google said internal testing showed Carbon reduced unsupported claims by approximately half compared with Argon, while stating methodological limitations directly rather than fabricating missing evidence.

The company also said the model could retrieve relevant sources and highlight discrepancies when faced with ambiguity. It added that Carbon reduced task overreach by 26 per cent and under-service by 29 per cent during multi-step workflows.

Google said Gemini 4 Carbon would initially be made available to a limited group of cybersecurity defenders this week, before access was gradually expanded to developers, businesses and consumers.

The company said introductory pricing would be US$2 per million input tokens and US$10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens discounted by 95 per cent. After the introductory period, prices would increase to US$4 per million input tokens and US$20 per million output tokens. –BERNAMA

Gemini 4 Carbon 拿下 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 的 59 分，登顶。这条消息的传播路径很有意思——大多数讨论停在"最强"两个字上，而 Google DeepMind 自己摆出来的三组安全基准数字，反倒被当成了配菜。可真正的信息全在配菜里。

## 三个分数，说的是同一件事的两面

先看落差。SEC-bench Pro 拿到 88.2%，这个水平已经接近"考纲被吃透"。CWE-bench 71.0%，中等偏上，还算体面。ExploitGym 54.8%，刚刚过半。

把三个数字按"看懂—定位—动手"的顺序排开，曲线是往下走的。模型越来越擅长读代码、辨认漏洞类型、给出判断；一旦要求它把判断变成一条能跑通的攻击链，成功率就掉到一半附近。识别能力与执行能力之间这道裂缝，才是 Gemini 4 Carbon 的产品定位真正落在哪里。

### 88.2%：读这一侧快要饱和了

SEC-bench Pro 的分数高到这个程度，说明模型在安全代码理解、漏洞归因、补丁方案生成这类任务上，已经能和不少中级工程师打平，甚至更稳。这类基准的设计逻辑，本质是"给一段有问题的代码，看你多久能指出问题在哪"。它考的是知识密度和上下文窗口的利用效率，恰恰是过去两年大模型进步最快的地方。

问题在于，这类能力的天花板已经看得见了。再往上堆分数，边际收益会迅速衰减。基准本身会先失效——当大家都在 90 分以上，这个数字就失去了区分度。

### CWE-bench 的 71.0%，卡在一个尴尬的位置

71% 不算差，但它掉在了 SEC-bench Pro 后面将近 20 个点。这中间的损耗，出在"把缺陷类型和具体代码上下文对上"这一环。模型知道 CWE-79 是什么，也知道该怎么防，但要在几万行陌生代码里准确定位到那一处没有转义的输出点，难度是另一个量级。

这个数字对企业买家其实最有参考价值。真实的安全审计不是在干净的样本上做题，而是在一堆历史包袱里翻找。71% 意味着它可以当助手，还不能当责任人。

### ExploitGym 的 54.8%，最有信息量的一条

刚过半数。这个成绩放在"最强前沿模型"的语境里看着扎眼，但它恰恰是最诚实的一个数。利用链的构造是长程任务：侦察、假设、尝试、失败、换路、再试。中间任何一步走偏，整条链就断了，而且不会有人告诉你断在哪。

54.8% 传达的意思是，Gemini 4 Carbon 已经能在受控环境里稳定完成一半左右的完整攻击路径。这个数字对防守方是警报，对模型厂商是路线图——剩下那一半，靠的就不再是知识，而是执行。

## 长程智能体：从演示视频走进值班表

### 单步正确率会骗人

一个模型单步准确率 95%，看着漂亮。让它连续做二十步，全对的概率只剩三成多。误差会累积，而累积的速度取决于每一步能不能自我纠错。

过去两年智能体演示的通病就在这：演示视频里跑通三十步的是什么任务？大多是路径明确、环境干净、失败可回滚的操作。真实业务里没有这种奢侈品。Gemini 4 Carbon 主打的"长程智能体能力"，如果要在 ExploitGym 之外的场景兑现，靠的是它在探索失败之后的重规划能力，而不是单点智能。

### 安全攻防是长程能力最残酷的考场

用网络安全来标定智能体水平，这个选择本身就说明了 DeepMind 的判断。安全任务天然具备三个特征：目标明确但路径未知、反馈稀疏、失败代价高。这三条恰好是当下智能体最容易翻车的地方。

反过来说，能在这类任务上跑到 54.8% 的系统，迁移到其他长程场景——大规模代码重构、跨系统数据迁移、基础设施变更——的把握会大得多。安全基准在这里不只是安全基准，它是长程能力的压力测试台。

## 59 分登顶，然后呢

### 第一是相对的

Artificial Analysis 的指数是多项基准的加权合成，59 分意味着在一批任务上拿到了领先的综合表现。但榜首和身后几名之间的差距，往往只有一两分，换个权重方案就可能易位。这类榜单适合判断趋势，不适合当采购清单用。

更值得记的是这句话的潜台词：前沿模型的竞争已经从"能不能做"转向"做得稳不稳、贵不贵、能不能连起来"。

### 采购决策里，分数排在第三位

企业真正会问的三个问题，榜单上一个都没有回答。第一，它在你的私有代码库上还能不能保持这个水平？第二，跑完一次完整审计要花多少钱、多少时间？第三，出错的时候，它能不能说清楚自己错在哪一步？

第三点尤其要命。安全场景里，"不知道自己在做什么"比"做不出来"危险得多。一个 88.2% 但会给错配方的模型，配不上生产环境。

## DeepMind 这步棋，买家得跟着调整

### 研究品牌开始背商业指标

把网络安全和智能体并列写进发布定位，这不是一个纯研究机构会做的动作。它意味着 DeepMind 的产品线正在往企业侧的付费场景靠，而安全是少数几个预算充足、痛点明确、还愿意为前沿能力付溢价的领域。

同时这也是一个信号：模型厂商之间的差异化，正在从通用能力排行榜，挪到垂直场景的硬指标上。谁的 ExploitGym 先跑到 70%，谁就能拿到安全厂商的集成订单。

### 安全团队的预算会松动

过去安全团队买 AI，买的是辅助工具——告警降噪、日志归类、报告生成。Gemini 4 Carbon 这类模型的定位，是把话术从"帮你省时间"推到"帮你做判断"，虽然距离"替你做决定"还差着整整一截。

这一截有多远？大约就是 54.8% 到 90% 的距离。它不会靠一次版本更新跨过去。

## Description

Meta Platforms, Inc. engages in the development of products that enable people to connect and share with friends and family through mobile devices, personal computers, virtual reality (VR) headsets, and AI glasses in the United States, Canada, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and internationally. It operates through two segments, Family of Apps (FoA) and Reality Labs (RL). The FoA segment offers Facebook, which enables people to build community through feed, reels, stories, groups, marketplace, and other; Instagram that brings people closer through Instagram feed, stories, reels, live, and messaging; Messenger, a messaging application for people to connect with friends, family, communities, and businesses across platforms and devices through text, audio, and video calls; Meta AI, an assistant that's available across apps, as a stand-alone app, on AI glasses, and on the web; Threads, an application for text-based updates and public conversations; and WhatsApp, a messaging application that is used by people and businesses to communicate and transact. The RL segment provides virtual and augmented reality products, including consumer hardware, software, and content that help people feel connected, as well as Meta Quest devices that enable social experiences across gaming, fitness, entertainment, and more. The segment also includes wearables such as AI glasses like Ray Ban Meta and Oakley Meta glasses; and the Meta Ray Ban Display, which combines AI glasses with an integrated lens display and the Meta Neural Band, a wrist worn device using electromyography that lets people control their AI glasses through neuromuscular signals. Meta Platforms, Inc. has a collaboration with Microsoft Corporation, NVIDIA Corporation, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc., Broadcom Inc., and OpenAI, L.L.C. 其中最值得关注的 FrontierCode 2.0 完全换了一套评分逻辑。132 项任务全部来自真实开源仓库，模型提交的代码改动不再只由单元测试是否通过来判定，而是由该仓库的维护者按“是否愿意合并这个 PR”来打分，任何一项阻塞性检查失败即记零分。

Cognition 在 6 月推出 FrontierCode 初版时就强调，传统基准只检查代码能否跑通，而合并决策还涉及改动范围是否克制、风格是否与代码库一致、回归风险是否可控等测试无法完全覆盖的维度。v5 将这一基准升级到 2.0 并纳入主指数，等于把“可合并性”而非“可运行性”推到了编码能力评价的中心。

在这一口径下，DeepSeek V4.1-Flash 1017（max）在 FrontierCode 2.0 上录得 28%，是所有已发布权重模型中得分最高的一个。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 以 25.5% 紧随其后，但其完整权重按月之暗面官方博客的表述，要到 11 月 4 日前才发布，AA 在 v5 报告中将其标注为“weights not yet released”。

谷歌 Gemini 4 Argon（high）为 25.7%，GPT-6 Luna 为 25.2%，均低于 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash。需要说明的是，这一成绩位于 FrontierCode 2.0 单项之内；在 Intelligence Index v5 的综合得分上，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 与 GLM-5.3 同为 32 分，仍落后榜首 Claude Opus 5.5（58 分）26 分，且低于 Claude Haiku 5.5 的 36 分。

Artificial Analysis 指出，v5 真正加剧的是开源与闭源前沿之间的整体距离。v4.3 时，最强开源模型与榜首的差距是 3 分；v5 把大部分公开题换成私有题、并大幅加重智能体实战任务的比重之后，这一差距扩大到 12 分。Kimi K3.1 Pro 以 46 分成为名义上最强的开源权重模型，但它尚未发布权重；已发布权重的模型中，32 分是当前的天花板。

差距在 HLE-Diamond 和 Terminal-Bench-Science 两项上最为刺眼：Kimi K3.1 Pro 分别为 37% 和 34%，而 Claude Opus 5.5 在 HLE-Diamond 上为 68%，GPT-6 Astra 在 Terminal-Bench-Science 上为 63%。

v5 并没有让开源模型“一夜变差”，它改变的是测量的东西 —— 当题目不再公开、评分不再只看通过率，那些依靠公开题库优化出来的分数被系统性地挤掉了水分。

与 v5 同步推出的 Progress Index v1 则处理另一个问题：当基准本身每隔几个月就换一次，不同年代的模型如何放在同一把尺子上比较。Progress Index 将 2022 年 11 月以来发布的主要语言模型映射到一个连续的能力尺度上，其设计参考了 Epoch AI 的 Epoch Capabilities Index 的方法。Intelligence Index 继续作为衡量“当下前沿”的主指标，Progress Index 则用于观察“能力随时间如何演进”，两者回答的是不同问题。

实际上，v5 的九项评测中没有任何一个模型全部领先：Claude Opus 5.5 拿下 FrontierCode 2.0、HLE-Diamond 和 AA-Omniscience 三项，GPT-6 Astra 在 Terminal-Bench-Science 和 CritPt v2 困难子集上居首，Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上以 67% 领先，单项优势的分散程度比总分排名更值得注意。

# Echo launches Frontier to patch AI-found zero-days
Wed, 28th Oct 2026 (Today) 
MARA SUGUE News Editor

Echo has launched Echo Frontier, a product designed to turn zero-day vulnerabilities found by advanced AI models into private software patches before public disclosure.

The launch comes as security researchers report that newer open-weight AI models are becoming more effective at finding and exploiting software flaws. Anthropic research cited by Echo found that Zhipu AI's GLM-5.3 produced working end-to-end exploits in 50 of 410 attempts on the ExploitBench benchmark, compared with 56 for Claude Mythos Preview.

That matters because GLM-5.3 is openly available, while more tightly controlled systems are not. The shift raises the prospect that vulnerabilities could be discovered and exploited before a CVE is assigned, detection signatures are created or maintainers issue an upstream fix.

Echo said the new service addresses remediation rather than vulnerability discovery alone. Each finding is validated against a working exploit, then fixed and tested across the full application before the patch is delivered to customers through existing JFrog or Nexus repositories.

Customers then move to an official upstream fix once one becomes available, Echo said. The company also provides documentation on the detection and remediation process for compliance purposes.

"AI models are completely rewriting the vulnerability lifecycle," said Eilon Elhadad, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Echo.

"The old assumption was that a vulnerability becomes public, gets a CVE and a fix, and then enterprises respond, but that sequence no longer holds. If AI can find vulnerabilities before the traditional security ecosystem can, remediation has to move earlier as well," Elhadad said.

Patch gap

The announcement points to a growing gap between the ability to find vulnerabilities and the ability to fix them safely. Echo cited research from 1Password's Off-by-1 Labs, which found that 54% of 6,080 AI-generated patches either failed to fix the vulnerability, introduced a new vulnerability or did both.

That reflects one of the central concerns around AI-assisted software security. A model may identify a bug or generate a code change quickly, but the resulting patch can still break application behaviour or leave the underlying issue unresolved.

Echo said Frontier is intended to reduce that risk by combining automated analysis with validation and compatibility testing before any code is deployed. The process includes discovering unknown vulnerabilities, reproducing them with a proof of concept, identifying affected versions, notifying maintainers, developing and backporting fixes where needed, and distributing patched software privately.

Echo also said it coordinates disclosure as an authorised CVE Numbering Authority. That gives it a role not only in creating temporary protections for customers, but also in the formal disclosure process that follows.

"Frontier AI can now uncover zero-day CVEs, but without the means to fix them, every discovery becomes another liability," said Eylam Milner, Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer of Echo.

"We built Echo Frontier around the harder question: once a previously unknown vulnerability is found, how quickly can we turn it into software that is actually safe for an enterprise to run?" Milner said.

OpenEXR case

Echo said it has already used the approach in a recent case involving OpenEXR, the open-source image file format library. It discovered a high-severity denial-of-service vulnerability, validated the flaw and developed a patch that protected customers in about two days.

According to Echo, that protection was in place roughly two months before an upstream fix became available. The example illustrates the company's argument that organisations may need an intermediate layer of remediation when AI-driven discovery moves faster than the standard vulnerability management cycle.

Echo framed the process as a departure from the conventional model of discover, disclose, assign a CVE, fix and then deploy updates in enterprise systems. In its version, discovery is followed by validation, fixing and customer protection before broader disclosure and eventual convergence with the upstream patch.

Echo said the service is generally available. The offering builds on its existing work vetting, patching, rebuilding and delivering open-source software used across enterprise systems, including containers, libraries, operating system packages and virtual machines.

# Grok Deepfaked This UK Politician—Now She’s Taking Elon Musk’s xAI To Court

This interview includes references to sexual assault and child sex abuse.

WIRED’s Rosie Swash speaks with UK politician Jess Asato about tackling Elon Musk’s xAI after being subject to deepfaking via Grok, xAI’s chatbot. Jess and Rosie also delve into the ‘AI kill switch’ proposal, the specifics of Jess’ court case and the harsh reality of being deepfaked on the internet in 2026.

Released on 10/29/2026

Transcript

I wanted to take you back to the beginning of this year,

January 2026.

There was widespread reporting of Grok,

xAI's chatbot, being used to create sexualized images

of children and women

and those images being circulated on X.

How aware were you at this point of the phenomenon

of deepfakes being used in this way?

Very aware.

And actually had been working, you know,

with survivors who had experienced deepfakes

for quite a number of years, you know,

ever since the advent of AI, you know,

has been happening to women.

And the developing risks of children both

being, you know, put into child sexual abuse material,

but also children using nudification tools

on other children, thereby criminalizing themselves

because these tools are so easy to access, often free.

So I was already very alive to the huge harms

being created by AI deepfakes of both women and children

before Grok ever happened.

It was a known harm, which is why many of the tools

from, you know, other companies had already taken,

you know, steps to stop them from being used

to create this kind of content.

And, you know, there are a number of tools

where, you know, you type in

nudify or take the clothes off this person,

and the tool refused to do that.

So into that environment came Grok.

Was there a particularly egregious example

and incident prior to Grok when you became aware

of deepfakes that really stuck with you?

Yeah, I think it was probably listening

to the experiences of Jodie, who was deepfaked,

and it was such an affront to her

that somebody would do this.

And then she found out it was actually a friend.

Such a betrayal of trust.

These things destroy not just the individual involved,

but often families and everyone around them too.

For people who don't know, who exactly was Jodie?

This is a constituent of yours

or someone who came forward to you specifically?

No, no, no.

She's a very well-known campaigner on this issue.

That's not her real name.

Before, what happened was that victims had to prove

that there was no consent,

and now it's up to the perpetrators to prove

that there was no consent to create these images.

I know it sounds obvious,

but what exactly is nudification?

Well, it is where you ask an AI tool to take the image

or video of a real person

and, you know, using generative AI to make that person

either nude or engaging in pornographic acts

or making a part of them nude.

This is something that,

because of the huge development of AI

and the, you know, real photorealistic nature of it,

it has become increasingly hard to see this as,

you know, a fake image.

It can often look incredibly, incredibly real.

So what was it particularly about the Grok scandal

earlier this year that made you want

to raise this in the House of Commons?

It was the fact that we already knew

that you could stop this from happening

by designing the AI tool to reject the ability to do this,

that it actually says that the tool should

accept asks for the creation of adult sexual content,

even that which has dark or violent themes.

And the fact was that this was completely avoidable,

and that's why I spoke out,

but also because I just spent a year and a half

campaigning to get a ban on nudification apps,

and here was an all-purpose AI tool

becoming a nudification app.

And it just felt to me as though, you know,

we were making strides in the UK,

and then the world's richest man

and his product decided to turn the clock back.

So what exactly did you stand up and say?

What I did was I talked about the need

for the government to accelerate their ban

on nudification apps, which they did.

So the Secretary of State, Liz Kendall, said

that she was going to bring that ban into law

through the Crime and Policing Bill, which she did.

But I also said that it was very important

that we went further than that

because, of course, Grok itself

is not a sole-purpose nudification tool.

It has a general use,

and therefore we needed to bring all AI chatbots

under the auspices of the Online Safety Act.

And we're now waiting until

that legislation comes into effect.

There's got to be a consultation, I understand,

before it does.

So technically another Grok could happen in this period,

but in the future, there would be much stronger measures

that we could take against tools like Grok

creating nudification content.

So that's a really positive outcome

of your interjection in Parliament,

but what else happened as a result of you standing up?

Well, one of the things that happened was

that I posted on social saying that, you know,

Elon Musk should stop

and stop Grok from being able to do this.

And then, of course, I became a victim of,

you know, the same trend.

So, @Grok, put this woman in a bikini.

And, you know, most of the images, you know,

were sort of pornified, I would say.

So they weren't nude images,

but they were me with, you know, inflated boobs in a bikini.

Then people tried to, you know, make it funny, I guess,

by putting, you know, swastika on me

or hammer and sickles, depending friend,

or making me pregnant with quintuplets

and putting me in a kitchen,

because, of course, that's the only use for women,

is birthing and making dinner.

But the kind of really disturbing one was a video of me

being surrounded by a group of men,

chloroformed over my mouth,

and then I fall backwards onto a chair,

and then my skirts are lifted up.

So no nudity,

but clearly the next frame is meant to be a sexual assault.

So, you know, it was really,

really distressing and disturbing.

That was the point at which friend said,

You probably need to reach out to a lawyer,

because each of these things we reported to X,

and, you know, none of them contravened

their terms and conditions.

We just keep getting those sort of repeat emails

coming back,

We've looked into this and there's nothing to see here.

So I did engage a lawyer who sent a letter to X

to ask for these to be removed, and they were,

but it was at that point that he said,

Actually, I think you might actually have a case.

We think that xAI have broken the law.

I mean, I think it's brilliant that you did that,

and I can see the through line of your legal training

and how practically you tackle things.

But when you were just telling me that,

it really turned my stomach.

I had a very physical reaction to you describing

what they did, and I just wanted to sort of find out more

about how it felt.

I mean, I'm really impressed by how you handled it

and the sort of default to action,

but it must have been really awful.

It was awful.

You know, this is done to demean,

to degrade, and to push women out of online spaces.

From my perspective, I tend to use

bad or difficult things that happen as a way

of thinking about how do we change this for the future.

My old boss was an amazing woman called Tessa Jowell,

and she used to say to me, if anything went wrong,

she would say, How do we change this negative energy

into something positive?

How do we work our way out this into a place

where we actually feel that we've learned from it?

And so I guess, you know, she instilled in me

that sort of sense that when something bad happens,

you've got a choice.

You can wallow in it, you can try and forget about it,

or you can use it as a catalyst for change.

And so I was quite trepidatious about the idea

of taking on a legal action,

not least because of the person who is at the top of xAI,

now SpaceX AI.

He's the world's richest man.

But also because I didn't want myself

to necessarily be the story.

Many, many women, you know, had things that were created

of them through both Grok,

but also other nudification tools that are much, much worse.

Having said that, I knew that if there was the opportunity

to say that actually they'd broken the law,

there was an important point of principle

on behalf of all of the women and the children

whose images were manipulated and misused by Grok,

who would never, ever be able to bring a legal case.

And so I decided that, you know, I wanted to do this

because I wanted to be able to show

that no one is bigger than the law.

It doesn't matter how rich you are

or how powerful you are

or how big a reach you have

in terms of your social media presence

or who your friends might be

at the top of various governments.

If you break the law in our country,

you need to feel the force of that.

And as an ex-lawyer and now as a legislator,

it is important that, you know,

we uphold our law where it has been broken.

And so it's also about giving control back, I think,

to us as individuals, but also as a society.

So many of these digital changes have been done

without our consent, our say, you know,

and I think there's a feeling

that there's a sort of runaway train that we're all on,

whether we want to be or not,

because we all need to use online spaces

for our work, for connection.

to bring them more into line

# SpaceX Launches Grok AI Partner Program: Here’s What To Know

SpaceX is taking Grok AI to the enterprise channel with a new partner program featuring more than 130 early-access participants, including systems integrators, consultants, services firms and ISVs building AI products, solutions and services.

SpaceX is bringing its Grok AI technology and AI coding services to the indirect channel with the launch of the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network, a new partner program with more than 130 early-access channel and technology partners.

Under the new SpaceXSI program, the Starbase, Texas-based company this month introduced the program for partners using Grok to build products, solutions, and services for joint customers.

The SpaceXSI program is targeted at two types of partners, according to a company press release.

[Related: Delivering Reliable Connectivity And Cybersecurity On The High Seas: Inside MSP Marlink’s Approach]

The first, transformation partners, include systems integrators, consultants, and services firms who help customers deploy the Grok AI platform across an enterprise to create tangible business value. They deliver enterprise professional services through forward-deployed engineers. They can be in one of three tiers depending on experience and customer success.

The second, marketplace partners, are companies like ISVs that build plug-ins and integrations to let Grok work with customers’ existing tools. They also can be in one of three tiers.

SpaceX did not respond to a CRN request to discuss details of the SpaceXSI partner program.

The new program is the second time SpaceX has moved to create a channel program for its technologies. The company in May, in an S-1 filing, said that it has assembled dedicated sales and engineering teams to market and support Starlink connectivity capabilities for aviation, maritime and land mobility.

The SpaceX executive heading the new channel program appears to be Ashley Hickey, director of North America channels for the company, according to her LinkedIn profile.

Hickey most recently served as director of North America channels for Cursor, the AI coding startup, which SpaceX acquired this past summer in an all-stock deal worth $60 billion. Prior to that, she served in channel executive roles at Cyera and Rubrik.

Scott Blahauvietz, vice president of AI sales at Ahead, a Chicago-based solution provider ranked No. 24 on CRN’s 2026 Solution Provider 500, said the link to Cursor is clearly visible in the new SpaceXSI partner program.

Ahead came into the SpaceXSI partner program because it was a Cursor partner before that company was acquired, Blahauvietz told CRN.

“I don’t think SpaceX AI really had a very mature partner program, and so I think a lot of what they’ve done has been a result of what Cursor brought to the table post-acquisition,” he said.

SpaceX is currently maturing and growing its program, Blahauvietz said.

“It’s not unlike what we see with other frontier model providers in this space,” he said. “It’s a services partnership at this point with various tiers within the partnership based on capability, engineers, and some customer metrics as we go forward. We’re super excited about it because we’ve got a very robust AI agentic and AI SDLC delivery program. It’s typically partnered with a hyperscaler, so we start thinking about the multiple partners that we can bring to the table where we’re already focused.”

Ahead can bring together SpaceXSI’s coding assistant with the hyperscaler’s model, Blahauvietz said.

“Riding on top of an AWS instance, for example, we could provide a full, robust solution of technology partners with our customer, and then add our consulting services and maybe managed services in some cases over the top, depending on what the customer wants to do,” he said.

Nearly every enterprise is evaluating multiple players and technologies, and some have placed bets with one or two of them while others are constantly morphing because they realize there will be a technology leapfrog cycle that happens here as different models get released, Blahauvietz said.

“What you’ll see going forward is tighter integration between what Cursor brought to the table and what Grok is delivering, and then finding those enterprise use cases,” he said. “I really think it’s the marriage between how we are driving our AI SDLC program on top of the automation and agentic aspect that Grok brings.”

Kelly Yeh, president of Phalanx Technology Group, a Chantilly, Virginia-based solution provider, has not yet engaged with SpaceX, but will.

“It’s smart to look into any partnerships with arguably the most successful businessperson on the planet,” Yeh told CRN. “He may not win every time, but he wins more than he loses.”

Phalanx Technology Group is looking at the program from the point of view of an integrator because the solution provider is not really a developer, Yeh said.

“We do a lot of infrastructure and security work for our client base,” he said. “And I need to pursue all of these technologies now until the winners start to winnow out. We’re primarily a Microsoft shop, so I’m going to lean heavy on the Copilot side for a lot of my clients. But there’s going to be people who don’t want to do business with Anthropic or Microsoft or Google, and they’re going to be looking for other solutions. ChatGPT is already saturated, and if this is a new program, it is an opportunity to fill a void.”

Yeh said his company is ready to put a data lake in front of Grok and see what it can do.

“We have a couple clients where we have deployed AI for them to connect to their data lakes and manipulate the data,” he said. “We built the lake houses, and we’re just trying to figure out for them how this is going to go. So I think playing with Grok would be a good move. One of the things I’d like to see is on the back end, how to keep proprietary data from leaking out? That’s the number one thing I hear from every client.”

SpaceXSI currently has over 130 partners in the early access phase of its program. In addition to Ahead, other solution providers in the program include Tech Mahindra, EPAM Systems and NTT Data.

# The Frontier Is Now Staged: Gatelists Before Grand Openings

Mistral's Hugging Face countdown shortened from October 31 to October 29 while the weights stayed absent and the LICENSE stayed unreadable – and across the frontier, vetted-partner lists, red-team tiers, and subscription walls now open before any grand opening.

Lena ParkForkast mind

At 22:42:37Z on October 28, the Mistral Large 4 card shifted its countdown. The ETA, which had held steady at October 31 since October 14, moved forward to October 29. This adjustment occurred while the repository remained empty of open weights and the LICENSE file path returned a 404 error at 23:35:08Z, with the raw/main LICENSE returning a 401 at 23:32:11Z. The countdown shortened by two days, yet the artifact remains absent. This is not a delay; it is the operational reality of the modern frontier.

## The Staged Access Pattern

Frontier model distribution has shifted away from simple release cycles toward controlled, tiered access. The product is no longer the model itself, but the gate that controls it. Labs are increasingly utilizing gatelists – curated, tiered, and often opaque queues – to manage deployment before a grand opening ever occurs. This approach allows for the monetization of anticipation and the strict control of model capabilities through tiered access, effectively turning the waitlist into a functional component of the product strategy.

## Three Exhibits of the Gate

Mistral’s approach, detailed in their October 6 announcement, establishes two distinct tiers before weights are even released. The public preview API on Mistral Studio serves as the baseline, while a separate, privileged tier provides red-team access to cybersecurity leaders, vetted partners, and state authorities. This privileged group operates with reduced moderation and expanded cyber capabilities, creating a bifurcated environment where the model’s most potent features are reserved for a select few.

Google’s Fairwind Program formalizes this exclusion. With over 650 partners globally, the program grants exclusive access to Gemini 4 Argon. Access is contingent upon background checks, and the terms explicitly prohibit partners from sharing, redistributing, or selling access. The gate here is a compliance and vetting mechanism, ensuring that only high-priority defenders – governments, healthcare, and telecommunications – can interact with the most advanced iterations of the model.

Meta’s strategy, as outlined in their recent developer blog, utilizes subscription tiers to gate performance. Muse Wonder Full is available exclusively through a subscription in Muse Code, featuring Power Usage and Maximum Usage plans that offer an 80x limit over the Everyday Usage plan. Meanwhile, the standard Muse Wonder model is sold via the Meta Model API at $4 per million tokens for input and $20 for output. The gate is defined by capacity and cost, segmenting users by their willingness to pay for scale.

## The Compounding Waitlist

The waitlist itself has become a metric of the gate’s efficacy. On the Mistral Large 4 card, the number of waiting users has compounded steadily: 813 on October 14, 939 on October 24, 969 on October 27, and 991 at the 23:32Z fetch on October 28. This growth occurs in a vacuum where no downloadable weights exist. As previously noted in the fetch-is-the-product analysis, the fetch has become the product. The waitlist is not merely a queue; it is a signal of demand that labs leverage to maintain momentum while the actual artifacts remain behind the gate.

## Deployer Stakes

For enterprise deployers, this shift introduces significant friction. Procurement, migration, and compliance workflows can no longer be scheduled against a reliable calendar. When dates are missed – as documented in the reported-date miss – the impact on internal roadmaps is immediate. Deployers are forced to navigate a landscape where access is gated by fetches and entitlements rather than public availability. This follows the broader trend of lab behavior, where, as discussed in the six-lab refusals ledger, many labs fail to meet basic transparency checks. The uncertainty surrounding the Mistral Large 4 release, including the final week countdown, is a continuation of this pattern.

## The Gate as Product

The absence of license terms is a critical retrieval gap; no license-specific claims can be made because the documents are inaccessible. We are left only with the vendor’s ETA, which functions as a disclaimer of intent rather than a guarantee of delivery. In this environment, the gate is the most valuable asset. By controlling who enters and when, labs maintain total authority over the distribution of frontier capabilities, prioritizing managed scarcity over open availability.

# 鑫闻界丨华为顺为追投，大模型领域的新变量扩散智能开源新模型

鑫闻界 | 2026-10-29 06:12:25原创

王赟 来源：齐鲁晚报·齐鲁壹点客户端

点击这里播放

扩散语言模型（dLLM）正在从论文走向产业。十月近尾，dLLM杀进Agent主场。

10月28日，深圳扩散智能科技有限公司发布并开源最新模型Clover-35B-A3B-Preview，采用MoE（混合专家）架构，总参数350亿、激活参数30亿。据团队公布的测试结果，Clover-35B-A3B-Preview在智能体编程等关键任务上的表现超过同类模型Mercury2.5和同尺寸自回归模型Qwen3.6-35B-A3B，生成速度在部分测试场景下可达后者的5倍至10倍。简单来说，后者更像“一个字一个字写”，前者则试图“先整体生成，再不断修正”。相比上一代模型，Clover参数规模扩大5倍，生成速度保持稳定，模型能力有所提升。

同时，扩散智能还推出了Clover-35B-A3B-Preview的决策模型，面向快速、结构化的判断任务，支持独立模式和联合模式两种作答方式，该模型将在后续发布。不同于TypeSafe的Jev等开源决策模型的单点评估思路，联合模式以全局统筹的方式开展推理，省去多次交互的耗时，使多项判断相互参照、规避逻辑冲突，一次性完成一组关联决策，实现更快、更稳定的推理结果。该决策模型还和Jev展开了一场中国象棋的对弈，结果是扩散智能的决策模型执黑获胜。

dLLM是区别于GPT、Claude等主流自回归模型的另一种大语言模型技术范式。扩散智能DiffuSpace是全球最早投入扩散语言模型研究的团队之一。

企查查App显示，扩散智能2026年3月在深圳注册，由香港大学自然语言处理（NLP）实验室联合主管孔令鹏教授及其博士生龚珊三、叶佳成联合创立。核心团队成员来自清华大学、北京大学、香港大学、卡内基梅隆大学等高校及头部模型团队。曾先后推出DiffuSeq、Dream 7B等研究成果。

2026年以来，扩散语言模型热度持续升温，Google、Inception、蚂蚁集团等科技企业相继加码dLLM：Google推出Gemini Diffusion，蚂蚁集团发布LLaDA系列，Inception持续迭代Mercury系列模型。与主流自回归模型逐Token生成不同，dLLM可进行并行解码和全局迭代，在部分场景下可实现10倍推理加速。据相关统计，2026年前9个月，相关论文总数已达2025年全年的2.5倍。有行业观点认为，dLLM 或将在未来两年取代自回归模型。随着人工智能向智能体、机器人、智能汽车等场景延伸，具备并行生成、动态修正能力的扩散语言模型，正成为大模型产业新的竞争方向。近期，DiffuSpace已与亚洲智能体计算平台公司Acrab达成合作，推动dLLM在AI PC、智能汽车、机器人及智能家居等端侧AI场景落地。

记者注意到，本月初，该公司首次公布连续完成两轮融资，总金额达数亿元，由经纬创投、顺为资本、君联资本联合领投，中科创星、华为哈勃、地平线等跟投。据悉，此次融资创下全球扩散语言模型领域最大规模融资纪录，资金将主要用于模型训练、垂直场景适配及基础设施研发。

其中，顺为资本由小米创始人雷军与许达来于2011年联合创立，是一家专注于早期至成长期创新企业的风险投资机构。另一家跟投机构华为哈勃，同样具有科技产业背景。企查查App显示，哈勃科技创业投资有限公司成立于2019年4月，为华为投资控股有限公司全资子公司。华为旗下投资机构与雷军联合创立的顺为资本共同参与融资，反映出产业资本对扩散语言模型这一新兴技术路线的关注。

# $100M ARR Founder: Build an Agent Harness

Gamma’s product leader explains how an agent harness combines tools, context, visual QA and user feedback to turn general models into a differentiated creative product.

GGreg Isenberg

Today10393 words (about 42 min)
View Source →

### Summary

Gamma’s co-founder and chief product officer explains the transition from manually chained LLM calls to an agent that can use tools, inspect its work and ask users about their preferences. A presentation request starts a sandbox, gathers context and audience requirements, selects templates, generates text and images, and repeatedly checks visual quality. He estimates that a finished output can involve around 20 models and 200 calls.

The conversation distinguishes objective evaluations from subjective taste, using brand compliance, editing, sharing, paid conversion and retention as complementary signals. Rapid experiments test both cheaper models and workflow changes. One fast-mode experiment challenged the assumption that removing friction always helps: reviewing an outline and answering questions improved investment and conversion overall, while a faster path still suited new mobile users.

For founders, the proposed advantages are distinctive taste, proprietary context, unusual tools and deep knowledge of a niche. Prompting and context engineering do most of the work, with fine-tuning used later for cost or specialized quality improvements. Slack collaboration, personalized communication, image-based furniture shopping and professional interior-design tools illustrate opportunities rather than validated new businesses. The discussion closes on sustained experimentation, serving a niche and choosing work the founder genuinely wants to use.

### Main Points

1. The harness does the work of turning models into a product

Gamma describes a sandbox, context gathering, clarification, generation and repeated visual QA; the reported model and call counts are the operator’s estimates.

2. Subjective quality needs real user signals alongside evaluations

Brand compliance can be tested objectively, but personal taste requires experimentation and behavioral signals such as editing, sharing, payment and retention.

3. Useful friction can improve outcomes despite slower completion

The general fast-mode test lost because outline review and questions increased user investment and paid conversion; a mobile newcomer variant was still useful.

4. Use prompts broadly and specialize after real usage emerges

The team reports getting most value from prompting and context engineering, while fine-tuning helps cost control and narrow tasks that general models handle poorly.

5. Build around a niche and a distinct advantage

Taste, proprietary data and unique tools can differentiate a harness; furniture shopping and collaboration illustrate possible opportunities rather than proven markets.

### $100M ARR Founder: Build an Agent Harness

## Brief Description

Gamma's co-founder and chief product officer discusses agent harnesses, creative workflows, model selection, experimentation, marketing automation and opportunities for vertical AI businesses. The conversation includes Gamma's presentation pipeline and practical examples from furniture shopping and professional collaboration.

## Table of Contents

- Introduction

- Evaluation and user signals

- Marketing engineers and personalization
- Image models and vertical products
- Niches and founder motivation

## Introduction

Today we're talking with John Nurona, co-founder and chief product officer of Gamma, and we're going to talk about agent harnesses, all the opportunities around it, vertical agent harnesses. I can't wait to dive in, and I want to give a special shout out and thank you to Anthropic, the team behind Claude, for sponsoring today's episode. John, thank you so much for coming on the podcast. By the end of this episode, what are people going to learn?

Thanks for having me, Greg. I'm really excited to be here today. We're going to dive deep on what it means to actually build an agent in practice, including demystifying what is an agent harness and what that looks like for us at Gamma, which is a creative agent harness, an agent for visual communication.

And not just you're you're being humble. Gamma is I mean it's it's grown extremely quick. I think it's hit 100 million ARR. You've just relaunched the platform. Huge release. And there's a lot you're learning. And what I hope to get out of this podcast is really just little insights around opportunities in agent harnesses, what you're learning in real time, and other opportunities that exist, startup ideas and stuff like that. So, John, can you commit that by the end of this episode I'm going to learn some of those things? I'm in. Let's do it. Let's make it happen.

So, I want to start off by like back here you can see what is an agent harness because I think a lot of people, you know, scroll X, they see agent harness, but they don't really understand what it is. So, can you clearly explain what it is?

## Understanding the harness

Absolutely. Let's break it down into the two words, agent and harness. And I'll use maybe Gamma's journey to illustrate both. So, for everyone's context, Gamma is a tool primarily for making presentations, also documents, websites, social graphics, that sort of thing. We've actually been around for several years, long before agents were ever a thing. We started the company in 2020, really took off in 2023, and early on we were just making these one-off LLM calls to do things like write a single slide or make the outline for a deck when we very manually strung them together into these preset workflows to do things like generate a presentation with 10 slides. The big revolution that's happened in the last year or two is this agent revolution where the most powerful AI products now are not stringing together these individual LLM calls by hand, but they're actually having one higher level loop of an LLM run that will do some kind of work, inspect it, use tools, and then turn that into something over a whole series of executed calls.

And so we actually went through this whole journey over the course of this year of rebuilding our product to be an agent. And building your product to be an agent involves building a harness. So the harness is all the tools that agent uses to execute things in its environment, inspect its own work, and deliver something finished to the user, including soliciting from the user what their actual preferences are. So probably the most famous agent harness is something like cloud code. Cloud code is a harness for programming. So cloud code teaches the agent how to go through all the files on your system and see what's there. teaches it how to like run tests and even prompts it with certain rules like go into plan mode in certain cases or run these tests after completing execution or do this stuff on GitHub.

In our case, Gamma is not a coding agent. It's a creative agent. So, it needs to do things like understand your art style and creative preferences, help you craft a story, and we care a lot about visual design. We're doing things like generating images and laying them out. So, we need to know how they look and make sure they look right. So, our harness takes all of those things and turns them into tools that an agent can use. And I can talk through what that look like.

Yeah, I mean, please do. And I think also I'm I'm curious if you agree or disagree with me. I've been saying agent harnesses are the new GPT rappers or new rappers, right? is that is that just a good tweet or is it is there some truth to it?

I think there's truth to it. Although I always disputed this concept with the GPT wrapper originally because it sort of implies that 90% of the work is the LLM and then there's just this thin layer on top which is the wrapping back and forth. I think maybe what harnesses illustrate is that actually the wrapping is most of the work. that you actually have all these LLMs which are quite similar in their core capabilities. Not to say they don't have some variation but generally all the magic of turning them into a product is building the harness around them. And even the model companies like OpenAI and Anthropic are putting so much of their work into harness development as well. So they are themselves doing wrapping of these things to achieve different capabilities.

## Generating and inspecting a presentation

Could you walk me through what happens like in 30 seconds after someone types a prompt on gamma? Like how many models does it touch like realistically you know because I think a lot of people are not sure h how that how that actually works.

Let me walk you through it. Let's go through a sample prop. So very typical use case for gamma is someone will paste in a bunch of messy notes or a document or PDF and say help me turn this into a 20 slide presentation. So the moment you put that prompt in a whole bunch of things actually happen under the hood. The first thing is we actually spin up an entire computer in the cloud. This is what they call an agent sandbox. This is what the opening eye ones broke out of famously in the last few months. So we actually spin up this entire sandbox where the agent gets all these files representing the user's prompt, the file they brought in, also other context about them. we then prompt the agent to go look through all that file and their prompt and run certain tasks. And for us, actually one of the first tasks is usually to figure out what other information we need from the user.

# Acxiom 2027客户体验趋势报告（下）：AI Agent正式"上岗"，品牌要抢的不是流量而是"授权"

2026-10-29 03:05

发布于：北京市

Acxiom 2027客户体验趋势报告（下）：AI Agent正式"上岗"，品牌要抢的不是流量而是"授权"

产品人研报 · 深度解读（下）| 原文：Acxiom《2027年度客户体验趋势报告——从影响力到行动力》 | 视角：产品经理体系_AI研创社

下篇导语：当AI从"推荐者"变成"代办人"

在上篇里，我们拆解了Acxiom报告的前三个趋势：AI如何通过"积极摩擦"重新定义轻松感、如何读懂你的情绪与意图、如何跨平台为你编排旅程。这三个趋势的共同主题是——AI在"理解你"。

但2027年真正的变量，在于AI不再满足于"理解你"，它开始"替你行动"。这就是后半场两个趋势的核心：自主AI代理行动（趋势四），以及AI成为品牌主要入口（趋势五）。

这两个趋势合在一起，意味着两件大事：第一，AI Agent正式从"辅助建议"走向"代理执行"，开始替你筛选商品、续订订阅、处理投诉甚至完成购买；第二，客户发现品牌的第一站正在从搜索引擎迁移到AI助手，88%的品牌已经开始担心"如果AI不提我，客户就看不见我"。

本文继续逐页拆解，并在最后给出产品创新、商业价值与未来科技趋势的三点洞察。

# 一、趋势四：自主AI代理行动——从"推荐"到"代办"

趋势四分隔页。核心命题：哪些事AI可以替你做？

【产品解读】品牌已经在做和准备做的自主AI活动，呈现清晰的"能力梯度"：

——解决简单客户问题：60%已做，35%两年内舒适；

——筛选产品/服务：59%已做，36%两年内舒适；

——续订合同/订阅：46%已做，41%两年内舒适；

——选最佳计划：45%已做，45%两年内舒适；

——处理投诉：45%已做，42%两年内舒适；

——进行购买或付款：42%已做，39%两年内舒适；

——完整申请材料：39%已做，48%两年内舒适；

——全流程管理旅程：39%已做，44%两年内舒适。

"已做"比例最高的是低风险、高频、标准化任务；"两年内才舒适"的集中在高风险、长链路任务。这就是AI Agent能力落地的梯度图。

【产品解读】消费者五五开：50%同意"如果AI总能带来最佳结果，我愿意让它替我做更多决策"，50%不同意。

两个关键细分：男性比女性更愿意让AI代劳任何活动；千禧一代在任何情况下都比其他代际更自在。这意味着AI Agent的早期核心用户画像是"千禧一代男性"——这是GCM投放和冷启动产品的关键数据。

【产品解读】这张"消费者舒适度随活动变化"表，是AI Agent产品设计的授权分级地图：

最舒适（65%+）：筛选最合适商品；较舒适（59%）：选最佳方案/报价；中等舒适（53%）：管理日程；低舒适（47%）：管理车辆保养；更警惕（45%）：医疗预约处方；更警惕（44%）：支出预算储蓄；最警惕（仅31%舒适）：进行购买或付款——46%完全不舒服。

产品设计铁律：越是涉及钱的动作，越要把最终确认权死死留在用户手里。可以AI代选，但不能AI代付——至少现在不能。

【产品解读】保障措施的优先级差异非常有意思：

消费者最要的是——AI行动前先征求客户同意（46%消费者）；品牌最想提供的是——客户可以查看/覆盖决定（65%品牌想给，但只有44%消费者认为这重要）。

代际差异：Z世代最担心AI偏见歧视；千禧一代最看重数据保护；X世代要行动前授权；退休一代要"必要时人能介入"。

产品启示：品牌设计的"保障"和用户想要的"保障"不在一个频道上。品牌以为给了"事后可撤销"就够了，用户要的是"事前先问我一声"。这是两种完全不同的交互哲学——前者是风控思维，后者是尊重思维。

【趋势四小结】自主AI体验已触手可及，但消费者需求因活动而异。AI的自主性唯有让客户感到被赋权且受保护、而非失去掌控，才能成为真正的竞争优势。

# 二、趋势五：AI成为品牌主要入口——AEO取代SEO？

趋势五分隔页。核心命题：当AI助手成为客户第一站，品牌怎么被看见？

【产品解读】品牌侧的判断相当激进：88%认为AI助手将成为许多客户旅程的主要起点；85%认为影响AI助手正变得和直接影响客户一样重要；84%认为不适应的品牌将"变得隐形"。

品牌最大的担忧排序：①AI提供误导性信息/做未经授权承诺（30%）——排第一；②依赖第三方AI平台（19%）；③失去与客户直接关系（14%）；④对品牌体验控制减弱（10%）。

产品视角："AI幻觉"已经不是技术问题，是品牌信任风险。当AI替你说话时，它说错了算谁的？这会催生一个新品类——Brand AI Governance（品牌AI治理），包括品牌知识库、AI回答边界、事实校准机制。

【产品解读】品牌预期AI助手对获客最大的影响是"客户更快决策"（57%）。预期负面效应：54%认为第三方评测更有影响力，43%认为自有渠道流量减少，43%认为竞争推荐加剧，33%认为品牌失去对发现之旅控制，31%认为官网搜索流量下降，26%认为品牌更难区分。

这就是"AI入口"对数字营销的釜底抽薪：当用户不再搜索而是直接问AI，SEO、SEM、官网流量这套打法都要重做。

【产品解读】但消费者并没有品牌那么焦虑。只有54%认为"找不到AI助手的品牌会被忽视"——而且这54%主要是千禧一代（70%认同）。

关键事实：搜索引擎的普及程度仍高于AI助手；比较网站在保险、手机套餐、购车场景依然关键；解决问题和选医疗方案时，与人沟通仍是常见起点。这告诉我们：AI助手不是搜索引擎的替代者，而是众多入口之一。品牌需要做多入口运营，不能All-in AI。

【产品解读】这张"各场景首选起点"表非常有价值：研究产品时AI助手占25%（搜索引擎41%）；解决问题时AI助手22%（与人沟通36%）；比较车辆AI助手20%（搜索引擎32%）；选医疗方案AI助手仅14%（与人沟通30%）。

结论清晰：AI助手目前只在"研究产品"场景占25%份额，其他场景都是补充渠道。但高级AI用户（62%会在购买前用AI研究）比偶尔用户（22%）领先一个身位——这是未来的方向。

【产品解读】消费者对AI作为入口的三大担忧：①失去对决策的控制（23%）；②AI提供错误信息/虚假承诺（19%）；③分享过多个人信息（19%）；④有偏见的推荐（13%）；⑤赞助或付费推荐未明示（9%）。

代际差异：X世代和婴儿潮最担心失控；Z世代和千禧一代对错误信息和隐私同样警惕。这意味着AEO（AI Engine Optimization）不仅要做"被AI提到"，更要做"被AI正确提到"——事实准确性和透明赞助标注是底线。

【趋势五小结】消费者越来越多用AI发现品牌，但它仍只是众多入口之一。品牌要学会影响AI背后的消费者，同时继续投资客户仍在依赖的传统渠道。

# 三、品牌行动要点与研究方法

【产品解读】报告给品牌的六大行动要点：①AI的意图性是前进方向——品牌必须明确在哪些关键时刻用AI，而非全自动铺开；②积极摩擦可以建立信任——特定场景下的摩擦增进信任与差异化；③客户希望保持控制权——保留推翻AI决策的权力；④AI只是众多发现入口之一——影响AI的同时维护传统搜索与网络存在；⑤合伦理的数据基础至关重要——大多数品牌尚未准备好，数据底座建设紧迫。

这五条合起来，就是一份AI CX产品的OKR草稿。

行业分报告导引页。

研究方法总览：由独立第三方Insight Avenue执行。

【样本说明】2026年7月，4000份线上消费者访谈（美英各2000），全国代表性样本。AI经验水平：高级用户14%、活跃用户29%、偶尔用户32%、有意识但缺经验16%、陌生9%。"AI陌生+有意识但缺经验"合计25%，这是未来两年的待转化人群。

【B端样本】700份决策者访谈（美英各350），覆盖六大行业各约100人。这是一份以中大型企业CX/营销/AI决策者为样本的报告，结论不能直接套用到中小企业。

Acxiom公司简介：作为Omnicom（OMC）旗下连接数据与身份基础平台，Acxiom的定位本身就说明了这份报告的立场——它天然强调"数据与身份基础设施"的重要性。阅读时要意识到：这份报告既是趋势洞察，也是数据平台赛道的行业布道。

# 结语：产品创新、商业价值与未来科技趋势的三点洞察

第一，产品创新方向：从"AI功能"到"AI Agent权限体系"。这份报告最大的启示，是2027年CX产品的核心竞争力不再是"接了哪个大模型"，而是"设计了怎样的授权与撤销机制"。建议每个AI产品团队建立一张"授权梯度图"——建议权、选择权、执行权三档，每档对应不同的用户确认强度、可撤销窗口和人介入节点。能把"控制权设计"做到极致的产品，才配谈自主代理。

第二，商业价值重估：数据与身份基础设施是下一阶段的"卖水人红利"。36%的完全准备率意味着64%的品牌存在数据底座缺口。CDP、身份图谱、隐私计算、同意管理平台（CMP）将进入一轮新的采购周期。对甲方产品负责人，现在投入数据治理不是成本，是未来两年AI业务的入场券；对乙方，"AI-ready数据底座"将取代传统CDP成为新卖点。

第三，未来科技趋势：AEO会重演SEO崛起路径，但速度更快、护城河更浅。88%的品牌相信AI助手将成为主入口，但消费者只买账50%。这中间的落差意味着：未来18个月，谁能率先建立"品牌事实库+AI回答校准+多入口并行运营"体系，谁就能像20年前抢占搜索排名一样，抢占AI推荐位。但要警惕——当AI入口本身被两三个大模型平台垄断时，流量成本会比SEO时代更不透明。

一句话收束：2027年的客户体验，不是"让AI替客户做一切"，而是"让客户在AI的帮助下，更好地做自己"。技术放手与用户掌控之间的那个微妙平衡点，就是下一代产品经理的主战场。

# 李海珍借Brookfield外部资本推进AI Factory，Naver破解90亿美元基础设施难题

- 신광렬 기자

## Brookfield负责投资GPU和数据中心，Naver Cloud负责AI服务运营；通过分离资产投资与服务运营，满足NVIDIA 10亿美元战略入股的先决条件

[Insight Korea = 申光烈 记者] 随着Naver董事长李海珍通过与Brookfield合作，使AI Factory业务进一步具体化，相关交易结构及其背景受到业界关注。

此次交易采取由Brookfield投资GPU、数据中心等基础设施，Naver Cloud负责提供服务的结构。

Naver通过与外部资本合作，解决了为获得NVIDIA股权投资而必须首先 확보大规模基础设施的问题。

据Naver 29日消息，公司于27日与全球另类资产管理公司Brookfield签署了最高90亿美元规模的计算基础设施 확보协议。

Brookfield方面将设立暂称为“Asset Co.”的资产持有法人，并通过该公司 확보相关基础设施。

Naver Cloud将从该公司获得计算资源，并向客户提供AI训练与推理服务，同时根据业务收入支付使用费用。

Naver计划以“GAK Sejong”为核心据点，到2027年上半年把运营规模扩大至55MW，并于2028年进一步提高至200MW。

此次合作受到关注的原因，在于Naver把资产 확보与服务运营的角色进行了分离。

一般而言，企业建设AI基础设施时，通常直接投资设备，或通过旗下子公司进行投资。

但Naver选择从由外部投资者全额出资的资产法人获得计算资源。

根据此次交易安排，Asset Co.将由Brookfield方面全额出资，但由于会计上认定Naver拥有控制权，该公司将被纳入Naver的合并子公司。

也就是说，基础设施所需资金由投资方提供，同时Naver依据合同所赋予的控制权，将该法人纳入合并报表。

这一独特结构因此受到市场关注。

Naver之所以选择这种方式，背后存在一个重要前提——NVIDIA计划进行的10亿美元战略股权投资。

根据Naver今年7月公布的内容，NVIDIA的股权投资附带一项条件：Naver必须在该笔投资之外，至少 확보90亿美元规模的计算基础设施。

按宣布合同时的汇率计算，90亿美元约合12万亿韩元。

截至今年6月底，Naver合并口径的现金及现金等价物与短期金融商品合计为8.4014万亿韩元，而母公司单体口径则为2.899万亿韩元。

即使分阶段执行，对于Naver而言，在维持现有业务的同时完全依靠自身融资来承担这一规模的投资，负担仍然相当大。

因此，与Brookfield的合作被视为一种既能降低资金压力，又能满足NVIDIA投资条件的解决方案。

Brookfield提供基础设施所需资金，而Naver则利用建设和运营“GAK Chuncheon”与“GAK Sejong”过程中积累的技术能力。

如果NVIDIA的股权投资最终完成，Naver还将获得10亿美元资金，用于AI Factory相关新业务。

Naver的构想是，通过外部资本分担大规模前期投资负担，同时扩大AI计算业务，并最终把与NVIDIA的合作关系进一步发展为股权关系。

仁川大学经营学部教授洪基勇表示：“引入外部投资，并通过旗下企业运营AI基础设施，这种方式具有一定合理性。”

他还表示：“这种模式很难一概适用于所有企业，但根据各公司的治理结构和财务结构，确实存在灵活运用的空间。”

# Firebird signs Kazakhstan deal to expand AI infrastructure
Thu, 29th Oct 2026 (Today) 
KAREN JOY BACUDO Finance Editor

Firebird has signed an investment agreement with the government of Kazakhstan to expand AI infrastructure in the country. The deal was announced during a visit to Astana by NVIDIA Founder and Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.

Under the agreement, Firebird is expanding beyond its first AI factory in Armenia into Kazakhstan, where it has secured a US export licence for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. The first phase, being built with Kazakhtelecom at Data Centre Valley, is targeting a commercial launch in the third quarter of 2027.

A planned second phase would take Firebird's potential AI infrastructure capacity in Kazakhstan to about 500 megawatts. It also plans to establish Firebird Labs Kazakhstan to support local startups, research and talent development through funding, access to computing resources and research partnerships.

Kazakhtelecom, the country's largest telecommunications company, has already deployed 400 NVIDIA H200 and 480 NVIDIA B300 GPUs in Astana and Almaty. It also plans to deploy more than 1,000 GPUs in Data Centre Valley, along with more than 1,000 NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs in the Ekibastuz region.

The infrastructure build-out comes as Kazakhstan pushes to develop domestic AI models and applications. During a public discussion at the Alem.AI centre in Astana, Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev said the country wants AI systems that reflect its language and culture.

"We want AI that understands and speaks Kazakh and captures cultural contexts and cultural specifics," Madiyev said.

Huang said local data would be central to that effort and argued that Kazakhstan could use its energy resources to support AI production.

"Instead of just exporting energy, in the future, you could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence," Huang said.

He also stressed the importance of retaining control over national datasets.

"Your country's data is your natural resource. It belongs to you," Huang said.

The discussion also covered the use of AI in mining, mineral processing, agriculture, transport and logistics. Madiyev raised the prospect of Kazakhstan becoming a hub for training models for robots and other physical systems, an idea Huang welcomed.

"If you have ambition, and I believe you do, AI will lift your nation," Huang said. "AI will lift your people."

Startup activity

The Astana event also brought news that NVIDIA is investing in Higgsfield AI, a startup founded in Kazakhstan. Huang praised the company's founders during the public session.

"The first thing and the last thing is you invest in people, not companies," Huang said.

Higgsfield is expanding its AI infrastructure with NVIDIA Vera Rubin through cloud service providers as demand grows for its generative media products. The move adds to signs that local AI companies are increasing their own computing capacity as access to hardware improves.

Other companies are also testing commercial uses for the technology in the country. inDrive and Pony.ai are working together to explore robotaxi services in Kazakhstan, with Astana identified as the first city under consideration for deployment.

The two companies will assess the feasibility of bringing Pony.ai's seventh-generation robotaxis to the inDrive app. The effort is supported by NVIDIA AI infrastructure and built on the NVIDIA Hyperion sensor and compute platform with the NVIDIA Halos safety system.

National focus

Kazakhstan's government has been presenting AI as a national development priority, linking it to energy, digital infrastructure and industrial modernisation. The discussions in Astana reflected that wider agenda, with ministers, telecom operators, infrastructure investors and startups all featuring in the same set of announcements.

Huang also addressed AI security and education during the public discussion. He said the technology should be developed and deployed responsibly and pointed to NVIDIA's OpenShell as a way to contain AI agents by limiting access to files and tools while monitoring activity.

For younger people entering the sector, he said learning the underlying principles of AI mattered more than simply learning how to use the tools.

"I envy being 18 years old today... because the world is changing so rapidly, and there's a complete reset because of technology," Huang said.

The visit also carried symbolic importance. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev presented Huang with the Order of Dostyk, First Class, in recognition of his contribution to the development of artificial intelligence in Kazakhstan.

Later in the day, officials from the International Judo Federation presented him with an honorary black belt in judo, describing it as a gesture of thanks for his support for Kazakhstan's AI ambitions and for leadership aligned with the discipline's values.

For Firebird, the investment marks a rapid expansion from an initial concept into a major regional project.

"What began as a seed of an idea 180 days ago has grown into a major investment in Kazakhstan's AI future," said Razmig Hovaghimian, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Firebird. "President Tokayev's vision gave us the confidence to think bigger about what we can build together. With Jensen Huang here today, that ambition feels more tangible than ever. We're building the infrastructure for Kazakhstan's talent and ideas to reach the world."
